message.content:
Black holes are formed when *gravity wins* over all the forces trying to support matter, causing an object to collapse into an extremely dense region from which not even light can escape.[2][6][8]

The **most common** way this happens is at the end of a **massive star’s life**. The star runs out of nuclear fuel, its core can no longer support itself, and the core collapses; if enough mass remains, the collapsed remnant becomes a black hole, often after a supernova explosion.[2][6][8]

Other proposed formation routes include:
- **Mergers** of neutron stars or black holes, which can produce larger black holes.[1][6]
- **Direct collapse** of a large gas cloud, which is one leading idea for how some **supermassive black holes** formed.[1][2]
- **Primordial black holes**, a speculative class that may have formed from density fluctuations soon after the Big Bang.[1][6]

Black holes can also **grow after formation** by accreting gas, stars, and even merging with other black holes.[1][4][7]
